mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and increased borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS shows a sustained 3-month increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals supply chain disruptions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when INDPRO declines by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, inflationary pressures coupled with tight monetary policy lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong demand for housing and a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over two quarters signals a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when GDPC1 declines by more than 1% over two quarters.
